name: Boston free municipal library
description: The Boston Public Library provided a municipally organized free public library with a physical collection.

impact.note: One city gave residents free books at public cost, an improvement on subscription libraries, and served as a model for other American city libraries.

date.label: 20 March 1854
date.basis: Date of building opening in the institutional history.

events.statement: Boston Public Library opened its Mason Street building to the public on 20 March 1854.
events.scope: This documented community and episode; not a universal first.

evidence.supports: The library’s history dates its establishment and the opening of its first building.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the evidence gathered for this scoped capability, not global priority.

caveats: Earlier public and subscription libraries existed. Opening and the stated aim of free service do not establish actual use, borrowing eligibility, or equal access for all residents.

research.note: Initial source pass; independent review is outstanding. Independent review found a corroborating Digital Commonwealth summary for the 1854 building opening and approximate collection; borrowing eligibility and exact start of lending remain separate questions.

measures.subject: Boston Public Library collection
measures.conditions: Institutional historical account, approximate scale at the 1854 opening; not users or loans.

evidence.supports: History reports a collection of sixteen thousand volumes at opening.
